pages.title: The Quantum Zeno Effect
pages.text: $(thing)The Quantum Zeno Effect$()$(br2)Measure a system often enough and it never gets the chance to change: each measurement starts it over. Unlocks the Zeno Anchor, which keeps chunks loaded.

$(thing)Insight$(): 60$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Entanglement Links.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Entangled Photon Pair, 1 Clock.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A system that would leave its state on a timescale T is measured N times, evenly, over a time t. Write the chance P that it is still found where it started.
